absent: Numeric major number, CPU count and hotplug state values for MSR device registration
Behavior of MSR read, write, open and ioctl handlers beyond their presence in the operations table
Encoding of NMI categories and bound of the descriptor table
Layout of handler action records and register frames passed to NMI handlers
Platform reason port numbers, masks and clearing sequences beyond symbolic use
Ownership and wakeup protocol for crash rendezvous counters and shootdown hooks
Debug and tracepoint payload formats for NMI handler timing
Conditions selecting between the two crash-IPI helper builds

findings.text: Per-CPU MSR character device family with class-based device nodes; open, read, write and ioctl hooks serve accesses, seek is anchored to reject positions past the end, and per-CPU nodes are created when a CPU comes online and removed when it goes offline, with module unload reversing registration order.

Per-type NMI descriptor table entry holding a raw spinlock, an optional single emergency callback pointer, and a list head for chained actions; the table is indexed by NMI category and the fragments show four initialized categories for local, unknown, system error and IO check sources.

Per-CPU NMI accounting record with separate counters for normal, unknown, external and swallowed events, plus receive timing, entry sequence and ignore counters with snapshot copies for stall diagnosis and an atomic call counter.
This NMI translation unit enables local emission of tracepoint definitions.
A boot-time string option unconditionally arms the unknown-NMI panic flag and reports success, so any presence of the option selects panic behavior for unclaimed unknown NMIs.
Three global integer controls govern panic policy for unknown, unrecovered and IO-check NMIs, defaulting to zero-initialized state and consulted on the unclaimed paths before attempting recovery.

A global nanosecond threshold starts at one millisecond and is exposed for tuning through debug facilities; handler durations below both this threshold and the per-action recorded maximum are ignored, otherwise the per-action maximum is updated and a rate-limited notice is emitted.

The scheduling clock disables preemption without instrumentation, delegates to a non-instrumentable variant that dispatches through a static call target, then re-enables preemption and returns the sampled value.

External components register an NMI action for a given NMI category; the call validates that a handler is present and the action is not already linked, warns about duplicate internal system-error or IO-check chains, and inserts head-flagged actions at the front and others at the tail under lock using RCU list primitives.

Each NMI category descriptor has its own raw spinlock acquired with interrupt state saved to mutate the handler chain, while dispatch walks the chain under RCU read protection without holding that lock, allowing lock-free NMI-time iteration.

Platform NMI reason handling serializes on a global reason lock acquired by try-loop; while contended the waiter runs any pending crash-interrupt callback and relaxes, then reads the platform reason, processes system-error or IO-check sources, and releases before continuing.

Default NMI processing proceeds through ordered stages: microcode interception first, then CPU-local chained handlers with per-CPU normal accounting, then serialized platform reason handling for system-error or IO-check with external accounting, otherwise unknown handling with back-to-back swallow accounting; a local count above one arms a per-CPU swallow hint for the next NMI.

The raw NMI entry maintains a per-CPU execution state of idle, executing or latched; re-entry while executing only marks latched and returns, the first entry saves processor debug state, runs the default NMI body, restores state and either exits from idle or restarts once when latched was observed.

Raw IDT NMI entry completes guest NMI signaling, accounts entry, bypasses offline CPUs to microcode offline handling, implements the latch state machine around debug register preservation and interrupt-entry tracking, and preserves the page-fault address register across the handler.
A virtualization-specific NMI entry simply forwards to the common raw NMI entry with the same register frame.

A FRED-based NMI entry handles offline CPUs via microcode, preserves the page-fault address register across interrupt-entry tracking and statistics accounting, invokes the default NMI body, and restores the preserved register on exit without the latch machine used by the IDT path.

NMIs are edge triggered so concurrent arrivals can coalesce and only one can latch at a time; the implementation walks the full handler chain per entry and uses instruction-pointer equality plus a swallow hint to absorb a likely duplicate, at the risk of occasionally swallowing a genuine unknown NMI when combined with other events.

Unclaimed system-error and IO-check NMIs emit emergency diagnostics, optionally panic according to global flags, and otherwise manipulate the NMI reason port to clear or re-enable lines; the IO-check path additionally dumps registers and delays with watchdog touches before re-arming, so misconfigured flags can either panic or stall in NMI context.

Crash NMI handling ignores the crashing CPU itself, disables interrupts, runs an optional shutdown hook, disables virtualization extensions for the CPU, marks one fewer waiter for the crash rendezvous, then either uses a platform stop operation or halts in a relaxation loop without returning.

CPU stop removes the caller from the online set, disables its local interrupt controller and machine-check reporting, conditionally writes back caches when incoherence was flagged, clears its bit from the stop rendezvous mask, prefers a platform stop operation when present, and otherwise halts forever without returning.

Stall diagnosis provides snapshot and reporting helpers that capture per-CPU entry sequence, handler sequence, ignore and call counters for a mask of CPUs, then classify each CPU as progressing, entered-but-not-exited, or stalled with reason strings that distinguish handler presence, offline state and ignore mode plus time since last activity.

The crash-interrupt helper has two builds: one that invokes the crash NMI callback when a crash inter-processor interrupt was issued, and an empty build that does nothing, allowing the same call site to be compiled with or without crash rendezvous support.
A helper clears the per-CPU record of the last NMI instruction pointer, resetting back-to-back detection so the next NMI is treated as not consecutive.

A string module parameter selects MSR write policy by trimming input and mapping on, off and any other value to on, off and default modes respectively, with a readback that reports the current mode name followed by a newline.
Self-test outcome codes are small integers with success zero, failure one and timeout two.
NMI execution states are encoded as zero for idle, one for executing and two for latched.
MSR device naming uses class msr, per-CPU devices named msr suffixed with the CPU number, filesystem nodes under cpu with per-minor msr leaf, and chrdev registration label cpu slash msr.
